blocks.html:
Quick answer

India provides a broad range of breast cancer treatment options for international patients, including breast-conserving surgery, mastectomy, breast reconstruction, chemotherapy, radiation therapy, hormone therapy, targeted therapy and immunotherapy.

The appropriate treatment depends on the type and stage of breast cancer, ER/PR status, HER2 status, lymph-node involvement, previous treatment and overall health. International patients should ideally have their pathology reports, imaging and previous treatment records reviewed before travelling.

Treatment may involve several specialists, including breast surgical oncologists, medical oncologists, radiation oncologists, radiologists, pathologists and reconstructive surgeons. Depending on the case, treatment can be completed in one visit or may require several weeks or months.

The cost of breast cancer treatment in India varies significantly because treatment may involve surgery, systemic medicines, radiation, hospital care, investigations and follow-up. International patients should obtain a case-specific treatment plan and quotation rather than relying on a single advertised price.

blocks.text: A breast cancer diagnosis can be overwhelming, particularly when treatment needs to be arranged in another country. This guide explains how international patients can approach [Breast Cancer Treatment in India](/treatments/breast-cancer-treatment-in-india), from [pre-travel diagnosis review](/blogs/breast-cancer-diagnosis-tests-biopsy-er-pr-her2) through [treatment by stage](/blogs/breast-cancer-treatment-by-stage) and [follow-up](/blogs/breast-cancer-treatment-cost-in-india).
International patients considering India usually need answers to several practical questions:

items: Can my pathology be reviewed before I travel?
Can chemotherapy or radiation be arranged in India?
How long should I stay in India?
What happens after I return home?

blocks.label: Send your records for a pre-travel review

blocks.alt: International patient with a medical folder, imaging tablet and suitcase meeting a clinician before treatment in India
blocks.caption: Treatment planning should start with a complete file: pathology, ER/PR/HER2, imaging and previous treatment records.

blocks.text: Why Do International Patients Consider India for Breast Cancer Treatment?

India has hospitals providing multiple cancer-treatment specialties under one healthcare system. Multidisciplinary teams in [Delhi NCR](/doctors/India/Delhi-NCR), [Mumbai](/doctors/India/Mumbai), [Bengaluru](/doctors/India/Bengaluru), [Chennai](/doctors/India/Chennai) and [Hyderabad](/doctors/India/Hyderabad) can coordinate surgery, systemic therapy and radiation.
Depending on the hospital, patients may have access to:

items: Genetic and molecular testing where clinically indicated

blocks.text: For a patient who needs several treatment modalities, having these services coordinated within the same hospital or healthcare network can simplify the treatment pathway. Patients should evaluate hospitals and treatment teams based on their specific diagnosis and treatment requirements, rather than assuming that every hospital offers the same services.
What Breast Cancer Treatments Are Available in India?
Treatment depends on the individual cancer. Potential treatments include:

**Surgery:** [breast-conserving surgery](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Lumpectomy) (lumpectomy), [mastectomy](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Mastectomy), [nipple-sparing mastectomy](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Nipple-Sparing-Mastectomy) in selected patients, sentinel lymph node biopsy, axillary lymph node surgery where indicated, [oncoplastic breast surgery](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Oncoplastic-Breast-Surgery) and [breast reconstruction](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Breast-Reconstruction).

**Medical oncology:** [chemotherapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Chemotherapy), [hormone therapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Hormone-Therapy), [HER2-targeted therapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Targeted-Therapy), [immunotherapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Immunotherapy) in selected cancers, and other systemic treatments depending on tumour biology.

**Radiation oncology:** [radiation](/costs/India/Radiation-Oncology/EBRT) after breast-conserving surgery, post-mastectomy radiation for selected patients, and radiation for certain advanced or metastatic situations.
Not every patient needs all of these treatments.
The First Step: Get Your Diagnosis Reviewed

For an international patient, treatment planning should ideally begin before travelling to India. The treating team needs to understand the [diagnosis](/blogs/breast-cancer-diagnosis-tests-biopsy-er-pr-her2) as accurately as possible.

Important records may include the biopsy report, histopathology report, ER, PR and HER2 reports, mammography, breast ultrasound, breast MRI if performed, CT scans, PET-CT where clinically indicated, bone scans where applicable, previous surgery records, chemotherapy records, radiation treatment records and previous medication history.
The hospital may request digital copies of imaging studies rather than only written reports.
[WhatsApp your pathology and imaging file](https://wa.me/919044346292?text=I%20would%20like%20to%20send%20my%20breast%20cancer%20records%20for%20a%20pre-travel%20review%20in%20India.)
Why Pathology Review Is Important

Breast cancer is not one single disease. Treatment can differ substantially according to histological type, tumour grade, ER status, PR status, HER2 status, tumour size, lymph-node status, stage and other pathological or molecular findings.

For this reason, a diagnosis such as "breast cancer" alone is usually not enough to create a complete treatment plan. The oncology team may review existing pathology and, when clinically appropriate, request additional testing. See [how diagnosis is built](/blogs/breast-cancer-diagnosis-tests-biopsy-er-pr-her2) and [what ER, PR and HER2 mean](/blogs/er-pr-her2-breast-cancer-treatment-india).
Understanding ER, PR and HER2
Three important biomarkers commonly considered in breast cancer treatment are:

items: Estrogen Receptor (ER) — an ER-positive tumour may respond to endocrine or hormone therapy.
Progesterone Receptor (PR) — PR status provides additional information about tumour biology and treatment planning.
HER2 — HER2-positive breast cancer may be treated with HER2-directed medicines.

blocks.text: A patient may have ER-positive / HER2-negative cancer, ER-positive / HER2-positive cancer, ER-negative / HER2-positive cancer, triple-negative breast cancer, or other combinations. These distinctions can significantly affect the [treatment pathway](/blogs/er-pr-her2-breast-cancer-treatment-india).
How Is Breast Cancer Staged?
Before treatment is finalized, doctors determine how extensive the cancer is. Staging may consider primary tumour size, lymph-node involvement, spread to distant organs and tumour biology.

Breast cancer is commonly described using [stages from 0 through 4](/blogs/breast-cancer-stages-0-1-2-3-4). The treatment approach for an early-stage tumour can be very different from treatment for metastatic disease. See [treatment by stage](/blogs/breast-cancer-treatment-by-stage).
What Happens After an International Patient Contacts a Hospital?

blocks.alt: Four moments of the same patient: arriving with a suitcase, consulting a doctor, receiving an infusion, then leaving with discharge records
blocks.caption: A typical pathway: records review, in-person consultation, treatment, then a written summary for home-country follow-up.

blocks.text: The exact process varies between hospitals and medical-tourism facilitators, but a typical pathway may look like:
This sequence may change if the medical team needs additional information before making a recommendation.
Can Doctors in India Review My Case Before I Travel?

In many situations, medical records can be reviewed before an international patient travels. This can be particularly useful when the patient has already undergone biopsy, surgery, chemotherapy, radiation, targeted therapy or hormone therapy.

Pre-travel review may help clarify whether the patient is likely to require surgery, additional systemic treatment, radiation, reconstruction, further diagnostic testing or a second opinion. It does not replace the in-person examination when one is required.
[Ask GAF to review your case before travel](/consult?treatment=Breast%20Cancer%20Treatment%20in%20India)
Breast Cancer Surgery in India

blocks.alt: Two patients standing with a surgeon and a reconstructive specialist holding an implant model
blocks.caption: Surgical options range from breast-conserving surgery to mastectomy and reconstruction. The choice follows the diagnosis, not a single advertised procedure.

blocks.text: Surgery is an important part of treatment for many patients with localized breast cancer. Depending on the diagnosis, surgical options may include:
Lumpectomy

Lumpectomy removes the tumour along with a margin of surrounding tissue while preserving most of the breast. It is generally followed by [radiation therapy](/costs/India/Radiation-Oncology/EBRT) when breast-conserving treatment is appropriate.

- [Breast-Conserving Surgery Doctors in India](/doctors/India/Surgical-Oncology/Lumpectomy)
- [Lumpectomy cost in India](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Lumpectomy)
Mastectomy
Mastectomy removes most or all of the breast tissue. It may be appropriate in several clinical situations. Reconstruction can sometimes be performed at the same time or later.

- [Mastectomy Doctors in India](/doctors/India/Surgical-Oncology/Mastectomy)
- [Mastectomy cost in India](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Mastectomy)
Nipple-Sparing Mastectomy
In selected patients, the nipple-areola complex and some breast skin can be preserved while the underlying breast tissue is removed. This may be combined with reconstruction.

- [Nipple-Sparing Mastectomy Doctors in India](/doctors/India/Surgical-Oncology/Nipple-Sparing-Mastectomy)
- [Nipple-sparing mastectomy cost](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Nipple-Sparing-Mastectomy)
Oncoplastic Breast Surgery

Oncoplastic techniques combine cancer surgery with reconstructive principles to improve breast shape following tumour removal. They may be considered for selected patients undergoing breast-conserving surgery.

- [Oncoplastic Breast Surgery Doctors in India](/doctors/India/Surgical-Oncology/Oncoplastic-Breast-Surgery)
- [Oncoplastic surgery cost](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Oncoplastic-Breast-Surgery)
Breast Reconstruction
Reconstruction can be performed during or after mastectomy. Options may include implant-based reconstruction, tissue-based reconstruction and staged reconstruction.

- [Breast Reconstruction Doctors in India](/doctors/India/Surgical-Oncology/Breast-Reconstruction)
- [Breast reconstruction cost](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Breast-Reconstruction)
[Ask whether surgery is likely in your case](/consult?treatment=Breast%20Cancer%20Treatment%20in%20India)
Chemotherapy for International Patients
Chemotherapy may be recommended before surgery, after surgery, for advanced breast cancer, or in combination with targeted treatment. The exact regimen depends on cancer subtype and stage.

Chemotherapy is usually delivered in cycles, with treatment and recovery periods between administrations. For international patients, the number of planned cycles is particularly important because it can influence how long they need to remain in India.

- [Chemotherapy Doctors in India](/doctors/India/Medical-Oncology/Chemotherapy)
- [Chemotherapy Cost in India](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Chemotherapy)
[Ask about chemotherapy timing](/consult?treatment=Chemotherapy)
Targeted Therapy for HER2-Positive Breast Cancer

Patients with HER2-positive breast cancer may be candidates for HER2-targeted medicines. Depending on the clinical setting, treatment may involve medicines such as trastuzumab, pertuzumab and other HER2-directed therapies.
Treatment can be administered before surgery, after surgery or for advanced disease depending on the patient's situation.

- [Targeted Therapy Doctors in India](/doctors/India/Medical-Oncology/Targeted-Therapy)
- [Targeted Therapy Cost in India](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Targeted-Therapy)
Hormone Therapy

Patients with hormone receptor-positive breast cancer may receive endocrine therapy. Common medicines include tamoxifen, anastrozole, letrozole and exemestane. Some premenopausal patients may also receive ovarian-function suppression.
Hormone therapy often continues for an extended period, meaning international patients may continue this treatment after returning home.

- [Hormone Therapy Doctors in India](/doctors/India/Medical-Oncology/Hormone-Therapy)
- [Hormone Therapy Cost in India](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Hormone-Therapy)
Immunotherapy
Immunotherapy may have a role in selected breast cancer patients, depending on the cancer subtype and treatment setting. It is not required for every breast cancer patient.

The decision depends on tumour characteristics, stage, previous treatment, biomarker information, current treatment guidelines and individual clinical circumstances. International patients should provide their complete pathology and previous treatment records so the oncology team can assess whether immunotherapy is appropriate.

- [Immunotherapy Doctors in India](/doctors/India/Medical-Oncology/Immunotherapy)
- [Immunotherapy Cost in India](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Immunotherapy)
Radiation Therapy in India

Radiation therapy uses high-energy radiation to treat cancer cells in a defined area. It may be recommended after breast-conserving surgery, after mastectomy for selected patients, or for certain areas of metastatic disease.

Radiation treatment generally requires multiple visits rather than one procedure. The number of sessions varies according to the treatment plan. This is an important consideration for international patients planning accommodation and travel.

- [Radiation (EBRT) Doctors in India](/doctors/India/Radiation-Oncology/EBRT)
- [EBRT cost in India](/costs/India/Radiation-Oncology/EBRT)
How Long Does Breast Cancer Treatment Take in India?
There is no standard duration for every patient. Treatment time depends on the treatment pathway.

items: Surgery only — hospital stay, postoperative recovery and follow-up.
Surgery + chemotherapy — treatment may extend over several months because chemotherapy is delivered in cycles.
Surgery + radiation — radiation usually requires multiple treatment visits.
Neoadjuvant treatment — systemic therapy before surgery may require an extended stay before the operation.
Long-term endocrine therapy — may continue for years but can generally be continued after returning home.

blocks.text: Should International Patients Stay in India for the Entire Treatment?
Not necessarily. The answer depends on the treatment.

Some procedures require the patient to remain in India through the immediate postoperative period. Other treatments can potentially be coordinated between the Indian treatment centre and the patient's home-country oncologist.

For example, after a patient has completed the required in-person treatment phase, long-term endocrine therapy may be continued at home under medical supervision. For chemotherapy or radiation, however, treatment schedules may require repeated visits to the treating centre. The treating hospital should provide a practical schedule before the patient makes travel arrangements.

blocks.label: Ask how long you should plan to stay

blocks.text: Breast Cancer Treatment Cost in India for International Patients
There is no single cost for breast cancer treatment in India. The total expense depends on the treatment pathway. See the [complete cost guide](/blogs/breast-cancer-treatment-cost-in-india).

| Cost component | What may influence the cost |
| --- | --- |
| Diagnosis | Pathology, imaging and additional testing |
| Surgery | Type and complexity of surgery |
| Hospitalization | Length of stay and room category |
| Chemotherapy | Medicines, number of cycles and administration |
| Targeted therapy | Medicine selected and treatment duration |
| Radiation | Planning and number of treatment sessions |
| Hormone therapy | Medicine and treatment duration |
| Reconstruction | Technique, implants and surgical complexity |
| Follow-up | Consultations, investigations and monitoring |
A case-specific quotation is therefore more useful than a generic "breast cancer treatment cost." Patients can review the individual GAF Healthcare cost pages relevant to their treatment.
[Request a case-specific quotation](/consult?treatment=Breast%20Cancer%20Treatment%20in%20India)
What Can Increase the Overall Treatment Cost?

Several factors can substantially change the final expense: cancer stage, treatment type, drug selection, treatment duration, reconstruction, additional testing and complications. Unplanned treatment or prolonged hospitalization can increase the overall cost.
What Documents Should International Patients Bring?
Patients should create a complete medical file before travelling.

items: Passport identification details required by the hospital
Mammography, ultrasound and MRI reports if performed
Previous surgery reports and discharge summaries

blocks.text: Where possible, bring the actual imaging files rather than only printed reports — mammography, MRI, CT and PET-CT images. This can allow the Indian medical team to review the original studies.
Should Pathology Slides or Blocks Be Brought to India?

In some cases, the treating hospital may request the original pathology material for review. This can be particularly relevant when the diagnosis is complex, the treatment plan depends heavily on pathology, previous testing is incomplete, there is uncertainty about receptor status, or a second pathology opinion is required.

Patients should ask the receiving hospital in advance whether slides or tissue blocks are required and how they should be transported. Hospitals in [Delhi NCR](/hospitals/India/Delhi-NCR), [Mumbai](/hospitals/India/Mumbai), [Bengaluru](/hospitals/India/Bengaluru), [Chennai](/hospitals/India/Chennai) and [Hyderabad](/hospitals/India/Hyderabad) can confirm what to send.
What Happens During the First Hospital Visit?

The first in-person consultation may involve a medical history, physical examination, record review and a treatment discussion. Tests may be ordered if existing information is insufficient. The doctor explains the proposed treatment sequence and alternatives where appropriate.
Can International Patients Get a Second Opinion in India?

Yes. A second opinion may be particularly useful when the recommended treatment is complex, several treatment options are possible, major surgery is being considered, reconstruction is involved, the patient has recurrent or metastatic disease, previous treatment has not worked as expected, or the pathology is unusual or unclear.
For an effective second opinion, the complete medical record should be provided.
[Request a second-opinion review](/consult?treatment=Breast%20Cancer%20Treatment%20in%20India)
Multidisciplinary Breast Cancer Care

blocks.alt: A patient seated with a surgeon, medical oncologist, radiation oncologist, radiologist and pathologist
blocks.caption: Surgical oncology, medical oncology, radiation oncology, radiology and pathology often share one plan rather than working in isolation.

blocks.text: Breast cancer treatment can involve several medical specialties. A multidisciplinary team may include a breast surgical oncologist, medical oncologist, radiation oncologist, radiologist, pathologist and reconstructive surgeon. The exact team composition depends on the hospital and the patient's treatment needs.
How Should International Patients Choose a Hospital in India?

Patients should consider whether the hospital can provide the specific services required for their diagnosis. Important questions include whether the hospital has breast surgical oncology, medical oncology, radiation oncology, pathology review, advanced imaging, reconstruction if needed, coordinated specialists, international-patient logistics, a detailed quotation and follow-up after the patient returns home.
The right hospital depends on the patient's medical requirements rather than simply the hospital's overall reputation.
Questions to Ask Before Travelling to India

items: Has my medical file been reviewed?
Does the hospital need my original pathology slides?
Will I need additional tests after arrival?
Will I need targeted or hormone therapy?
How long is the expected treatment period?
How long should I plan to stay after surgery?
What is included in the quotation?
What medical care will I need after returning home?

blocks.text: Practical Travel Planning for Breast Cancer Treatment

Medical treatment is only one part of international travel. Patients should also plan for accommodation, local transportation, medical appointments, caregiver support, medication, recovery time, travel after surgery, follow-up visits and emergency contact arrangements.
Patients undergoing major surgery may need a caregiver during the initial recovery period. The treating hospital should advise when the patient is medically fit to travel.
What About Accommodation During Treatment?

Accommodation requirements vary according to treatment. A short consultation may need only a brief stay. Surgery may benefit from accommodation close to the hospital after discharge. Radiation and chemotherapy often require repeated visits, so staying nearby matters.
Continuing Treatment After Returning Home
Some patients can continue part of their treatment with an oncologist in their home country. This is particularly relevant for long-term treatments such as endocrine therapy.

Before leaving India, patients should request the final diagnosis, pathology reports, treatment summary, surgery report, medication list, chemotherapy details, radiation plan and treatment summary, targeted therapy details and follow-up recommendations.
What Should the Patient Carry After Treatment?

Before leaving India, patients should ideally obtain copies of the final pathology report, operative report, discharge summary, imaging reports and files, treatment protocol, chemotherapy records, radiation summary, medication list and follow-up plan. Keep these records securely because they may be needed for future consultations.
[WhatsApp GAF if you need a document checklist](https://wa.me/919044346292?text=Please%20send%20a%20document%20checklist%20for%20breast%20cancer%20treatment%20in%20India.)
Breast Cancer Treatment in India: Key Takeaways for International Patients

International patients can access a broad range of breast cancer treatment options in India, including breast-conserving surgery, mastectomy, nipple-sparing mastectomy, breast reconstruction, chemotherapy, radiation therapy, hormone therapy, HER2-targeted therapy and immunotherapy in selected cases.

The most important step is to understand the individual cancer diagnosis and treatment plan before making travel arrangements. Patients should ideally have their pathology, imaging and previous treatment records reviewed in advance.

The overall treatment duration and cost depend on the cancer stage, tumour biology, treatment sequence, medicines, surgery, radiation and follow-up requirements. For international patients, the goal should be to plan the complete treatment journey, not simply arrange one procedure.

Frequently Asked Questions
Can international patients get breast cancer treatment in India?
Yes. International patients can travel to India for breast cancer evaluation and treatment, subject to applicable travel and medical requirements.
Can my medical records be reviewed before I travel?
In many cases, hospitals can review medical records, pathology and imaging before the patient's arrival. The receiving hospital should confirm exactly which documents it requires.
What medical records should I send first?
A useful initial file generally includes the biopsy and histopathology reports, ER/PR/HER2 results, imaging reports, previous treatment records and current medication list.
Can I get a second opinion in India?
Yes. A second opinion can be sought from a breast cancer specialist or multidisciplinary team, particularly when treatment decisions are complex.
How much does breast cancer treatment cost in India?
There is no universal cost. The total expense depends on the diagnosis, stage, surgery, medicines, chemotherapy, radiation, targeted treatment, hospitalization and follow-up.
How long do international patients need to stay in India?
The duration depends on treatment. Surgery, chemotherapy and radiation have different schedules, so the treating hospital should provide an individualized timeline.
Can chemotherapy be started in India and completed in my home country?
In some situations, treatment can be coordinated between medical teams, but this must be planned in advance with the treating oncologists.
Can hormone therapy be continued after returning home?
Hormone therapy is often a long-term treatment and may be continued under the supervision of an oncologist in the patient's home country when appropriate.
Can breast reconstruction be performed in India?
Yes. Reconstruction may be performed immediately with mastectomy or as a delayed procedure, depending on the patient's cancer treatment and reconstructive plan.
Do I need to bring my pathology slides to India?
Not necessarily in every case. However, the receiving hospital may request pathology slides or tissue blocks for review. Patients should confirm this before travelling.
Can breast cancer treatment be planned completely before I arrive?
A preliminary treatment plan may be possible after medical-record review, but the final plan can change after physical examination, additional investigations or multidisciplinary review.
Can GAF Healthcare help coordinate breast cancer treatment in India?

GAF Healthcare can help international patients explore treatment pathways, doctors, hospitals and treatment-cost information in India. The final diagnosis and medical treatment plan are determined by the treating medical team.

Quick answer

Breast cancer diagnosis usually involves several steps rather than a single test. Doctors may use a clinical breast examination, mammography, ultrasound, breast MRI in selected situations, and a biopsy to determine whether an abnormal area contains cancer.

A biopsy provides tissue for pathology, which identifies the type and characteristics of the cancer. Additional tests commonly include ER (estrogen receptor), PR (progesterone receptor) and HER2 testing. These results are important because they help determine which treatments are likely to be appropriate.

Doctors also assess the tumour size, lymph-node involvement and whether the cancer has spread elsewhere to determine its stage. The final treatment plan may involve surgery, chemotherapy, radiation therapy, hormone therapy, targeted therapy or immunotherapy, depending on the individual diagnosis.

For international patients seeking treatment in India, sending the complete pathology report, biopsy results, receptor testing and imaging records for review before travel can help the treating team understand the diagnosis and plan the next steps.

blocks.text: Why Accurate Breast Cancer Diagnosis Matters
A breast lump or abnormal mammogram does not automatically mean breast cancer. Several conditions can produce similar findings, including benign breast changes.
Therefore, doctors usually combine:
The objective is to answer several different questions:

items: What type of breast cancer is it?
Has it reached nearby lymph nodes?
Has it spread to other parts of the body?

blocks.text: This information forms the foundation of the treatment plan.
What Are the First Signs That Lead to Breast Cancer Testing?
Breast cancer can present in different ways. Possible signs include:

items: A new lump in the breast
Thickening in part of the breast
Change in breast size or shape
Nipple discharge, particularly when it is unusual or bloody
A swollen lymph node in the armpit

blocks.text: However, some breast cancers do not cause noticeable symptoms. They may be detected through screening mammography before a person notices a change. Any new or persistent breast change should be assessed by an appropriate healthcare professional.
Step 1: Clinical Breast Examination
The diagnostic process may begin with a physical examination. The doctor may examine both breasts, the area around the nipple, the skin, the armpit and nearby lymph nodes.

The doctor may ask about when the change was first noticed, whether it has changed over time, previous breast problems, previous breast biopsies, family history, previous breast imaging, and menstrual and reproductive history where relevant.
A physical examination cannot by itself confirm breast cancer. Imaging and, when indicated, biopsy provide additional information.
Step 2: Mammography
Mammography uses low-dose X-rays to produce images of the breast. It can identify abnormalities that may not be detectable by physical examination.

Mammography may show masses, calcifications, changes in breast tissue, architectural distortion or other suspicious findings. The radiologist interprets the images and determines whether further evaluation is necessary.
Mammography is used both in screening and in the diagnostic evaluation of breast symptoms.
Diagnostic Mammography vs Screening Mammography
These terms can sometimes be confusing.
**Screening mammography** is usually performed in people without symptoms as part of breast cancer screening according to age, risk and local recommendations.

**Diagnostic mammography** is performed when there is a specific concern, such as a breast lump, an abnormal screening result, a nipple change or other breast symptoms. Diagnostic imaging may include additional views or be combined with ultrasound.
Step 3: Breast Ultrasound
Breast ultrasound uses sound waves to create images of breast tissue. It may be particularly useful for evaluating a lump or an abnormality seen on mammography.

Ultrasound can help determine whether a lesion appears cystic, solid, complex or suspicious. It can also be used to examine nearby lymph nodes. Ultrasound is often used alongside mammography rather than necessarily replacing it.
Step 4: Breast MRI
Breast MRI uses magnetic fields and contrast material in many situations to produce detailed images. It is not required for every breast cancer patient.

MRI may be considered in selected situations, such as assessing the extent of known breast cancer, evaluating the opposite breast in selected circumstances, assessing patients with certain high-risk factors, evaluating breast implants, or clarifying findings from other imaging. The decision to perform MRI depends on the clinical situation.
[Send your mammogram, ultrasound or MRI for a second look](/consult?treatment=Breast%20Cancer%20Treatment%20in%20India)
Can Imaging Confirm Breast Cancer?
Imaging can identify suspicious abnormalities, but imaging alone generally cannot provide the complete pathological diagnosis. A suspicious mass on mammography or ultrasound may require a biopsy.
The biopsy allows a pathologist to examine actual tissue under a microscope. This is one of the most important steps in confirming breast cancer.
What Is a Breast Biopsy?

blocks.alt: Gloved hands hold an ultrasound probe and a thin biopsy needle above skin, with a pathology cassette ready for tissue cores
blocks.caption: A core needle biopsy samples tissue under imaging guidance so pathology can confirm whether cancer is present.

blocks.text: A breast biopsy removes a sample of tissue from the suspicious area. The sample is sent to a pathology laboratory for examination. Different biopsy methods may be used depending on the lesion.
Common approaches include:
For many suspicious breast lesions, a core needle biopsy is commonly used because it provides a tissue sample suitable for detailed pathological assessment.
What Happens During a Core Needle Biopsy?

A core biopsy is usually performed using a local anaesthetic. A typical process may involve identifying the suspicious area using imaging, cleaning the skin, giving local anaesthesia, inserting a biopsy needle, removing several small tissue samples and sending the samples to pathology.
The exact method depends on whether the lesion is best visualized by ultrasound, mammography, MRI or another imaging technique.
Does a Breast Biopsy Spread Cancer?
This is a common concern. A properly performed diagnostic biopsy is an established part of breast cancer evaluation.
Patients should discuss individual concerns with their treating doctor, but avoiding a medically indicated biopsy because of fear that it will spread cancer can delay diagnosis and treatment.
[WhatsApp your biopsy report to GAF](https://wa.me/919044346292?text=Please%20review%20my%20breast%20biopsy%20and%20pathology%20report%20for%20treatment%20in%20India.)
What Does the Pathology Report Tell You?

The pathology report provides information about the tissue removed during biopsy or surgery. It can help establish whether cancer is present, the cancer type, tumour grade, invasive versus non-invasive disease, hormone receptor status, HER2 status and other pathological features.
After surgery, the pathology report may contain additional information that was not available from the initial biopsy.
Invasive vs Non-Invasive Breast Cancer
One of the first important distinctions is whether the cancer is non-invasive or invasive.
**Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS)** is a non-invasive breast condition in which abnormal cells are confined to the milk ducts. It is often considered an early form of breast cancer.

**Invasive breast cancer** means cancer cells have moved beyond the structure in which they originally developed into surrounding breast tissue. Invasive breast cancers require treatment planning based on their pathology and [stage](${STAGES}).
What Are the Common Types of Breast Cancer?
Breast cancer has several histological types. Common invasive types include invasive ductal carcinoma and invasive lobular carcinoma. There are also less common pathological types.
The exact type is determined by a pathologist based on the tissue sample. The type of breast cancer is only one part of the overall diagnosis.
What Is Tumour Grade?

Tumour grade describes how abnormal the cancer cells appear under a microscope and provides information about how the tumour is behaving biologically. Breast cancers are commonly assigned Grade 1, Grade 2 or Grade 3.
Grade is different from stage. This distinction is important.

items: Grade describes characteristics of the cancer cells.
Stage describes the extent of cancer in the body.

blocks.text: A cancer can therefore have a particular grade and a completely different [stage](/blogs/breast-cancer-stages-0-1-2-3-4).
What Are ER and PR Tests?

blocks.alt: Anatomical chest illustration with a tissue core moving into a cassette, then a microscope, then three assay wells for estrogen receptors, progesterone receptors and HER2
blocks.caption: ER, PR and HER2 are read from tumour tissue. The combination helps decide whether hormone therapy or HER2-targeted treatment may have a role.

blocks.text: After breast cancer is confirmed, the tumour is commonly tested for hormone receptors. The two major hormone receptors are estrogen receptor (ER) and progesterone receptor (PR). These tests help determine whether the cancer may respond to [endocrine or hormone therapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Hormone-Therapy).

A tumour may be ER-positive, PR-positive, both ER and PR positive, ER-negative or PR-negative. The exact interpretation depends on the pathology report. Read the full [ER, PR and HER2 explainer](${BIOMARKERS}).
Why Is ER Status Important?
Estrogen can stimulate the growth of some breast cancer cells. If a tumour has estrogen receptors, endocrine therapy may be an important part of treatment.

Common endocrine treatments include tamoxifen, anastrozole, letrozole, exemestane, and ovarian-function suppression in selected premenopausal patients. The treatment depends on factors such as menopausal status, cancer stage and recurrence risk.

- [Hormone Therapy Doctors in India](/doctors/India/Medical-Oncology/Hormone-Therapy)
- [Hormone Therapy Cost in India](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Hormone-Therapy)
[Ask whether hormone therapy applies](/consult?treatment=Hormone%20Therapy)
What Is HER2?
HER2 stands for human epidermal growth factor receptor 2. HER2 is a protein involved in cell growth and signalling. Some breast cancers have abnormally high HER2 activity.

These cancers are referred to as HER2-positive breast cancers when they meet the relevant testing criteria. HER2 status is important because HER2-positive cancers may respond to [HER2-targeted treatment](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Targeted-Therapy).
How Is HER2 Tested?
HER2 can be assessed using laboratory tests performed on tumour tissue. One common method is immunohistochemistry (IHC). Results can be reported as 0, 1+, 2+ or 3+.

A 3+ result is generally considered HER2-positive. An IHC 2+ result is usually considered equivocal and may require additional testing, such as in situ hybridization (ISH), depending on the pathology process. The treating team should interpret the result in the context of the complete pathology report.
Why Is HER2 Status Important?

HER2-positive breast cancer can be treated with HER2-targeted medicines. These may include trastuzumab, pertuzumab, trastuzumab emtansine, trastuzumab deruxtecan, and other HER2-directed medicines in selected situations.
Which treatment is appropriate depends on the stage, previous treatment and clinical circumstances.

- [Targeted Therapy Doctors in India](/doctors/India/Medical-Oncology/Targeted-Therapy)
- [Targeted Therapy Cost in India](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Targeted-Therapy)
[Ask about HER2-targeted therapy](/consult?treatment=Targeted%20Therapy)
What Does Triple-Negative Breast Cancer Mean?
Triple-negative breast cancer refers to breast cancer that does not express estrogen receptors, progesterone receptors or HER2.

Because these three targets are absent, hormone therapy and HER2-targeted therapy do not have the same role. Treatment may instead involve [surgery](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Lumpectomy), [chemotherapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Chemotherapy), [radiation](/costs/India/Radiation-Oncology/EBRT), [immunotherapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Immunotherapy) in selected patients, and other treatments depending on the clinical situation.
Why Are ER, PR and HER2 Often Discussed Together?

| Test | What it assesses | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ER | Estrogen receptor | Helps determine suitability for endocrine therapy |
| PR | Progesterone receptor | Provides additional tumour biology information |
| HER2 | HER2 protein/gene activity | Helps determine suitability for HER2-targeted therapy |
These results are combined with tumour [stage](/blogs/breast-cancer-stages-0-1-2-3-4) and other pathological information to develop the treatment plan.
What Is Breast Cancer Staging?

blocks.alt: Transparent human body showing a highlighted chest site, a lymph-node chain under the arm, and internal organs used in staging
blocks.caption: Staging asks three questions: how large is the primary tumour, are nearby lymph nodes involved, and has the cancer reached distant organs.

blocks.text: Once cancer has been diagnosed, doctors determine how far it has progressed. The commonly used TNM system considers T (primary tumour), N (nearby lymph nodes) and M (distant metastasis). These findings contribute to the overall stage.

Breast cancer stages are generally grouped from Stage 0 through Stage 4. The [staging process](/blogs/breast-cancer-stages-0-1-2-3-4) helps doctors determine treatment and prognosis. Treatment itself is covered in the [treatment-by-stage](/blogs/breast-cancer-treatment-by-stage) guide.
How Is Breast Cancer Staged?

Staging may involve different tests depending on the patient's diagnosis. Possible investigations include physical examination, breast imaging, lymph-node evaluation, blood tests, CT scans, PET-CT, bone imaging, MRI and other investigations when clinically indicated.

Not every patient needs every test. For early-stage breast cancer, extensive scans looking for distant disease may not always be necessary. The treating team decides which investigations are appropriate.

blocks.label: Share your staging scans with GAF

blocks.text: What Are Lymph Nodes and Why Are They Tested?
Lymph nodes are small structures that are part of the lymphatic system. Breast cancer can spread to nearby lymph nodes, particularly those in the armpit.
Doctors may evaluate lymph nodes using ultrasound, needle biopsy, sentinel lymph node biopsy or axillary lymph node surgery. The findings can influence cancer staging and treatment planning.
What Is a Sentinel Lymph Node Biopsy?

A sentinel lymph node biopsy identifies and removes the first lymph nodes to which cancer is likely to spread from the breast. It is commonly used for selected patients with clinically node-negative breast cancer.
The removed nodes are examined by a pathologist. The results help determine whether cancer has spread to the lymphatic system.
What Happens If Cancer Is Found in the Lymph Nodes?

The presence of cancer in lymph nodes can affect staging and treatment planning. The medical team considers the number of affected nodes, the size of tumour deposits, primary tumour characteristics, ER/PR status, HER2 status and other pathological findings.
Lymph-node involvement does not automatically mean that cancer has spread to distant organs. This distinction is important.
What Is Metastatic Breast Cancer?
Metastatic breast cancer, also called Stage 4 breast cancer, means the cancer has spread to distant parts of the body. Common sites can include bone, liver, lungs and brain.
Additional imaging may be required when metastatic disease is suspected. Treatment is usually focused on controlling the cancer throughout the body, managing symptoms and maintaining quality of life.
Can a Second Pathology Opinion Be Useful?

A second pathology review can sometimes be valuable, particularly when the diagnosis is unusual, receptor results are unexpected, treatment decisions depend on a specific pathology finding, the original pathology report is incomplete, or the patient is seeking a second opinion abroad.

For international patients, the receiving hospital may review the existing pathology material or request additional testing. Multidisciplinary teams in [Delhi NCR](/doctors/India/Delhi-NCR), [Mumbai](/doctors/India/Mumbai), [Bengaluru](/doctors/India/Bengaluru), [Chennai](/doctors/India/Chennai) and [Hyderabad](/doctors/India/Hyderabad) routinely review overseas reports before travel.
Breast Cancer Diagnosis for International Patients Coming to India
International patients should ideally organize their diagnostic records before travelling. A useful medical file may contain:

items: Pathology: biopsy report, histopathology, ER, PR, HER2, Ki-67 where reported, and other biomarker or molecular tests where performed
Imaging: mammography, ultrasound, MRI, CT, PET-CT and bone imaging where applicable
Previous treatment: surgery reports, chemotherapy records, radiation records and a medication list
Other medical information: previous illnesses, allergies, current medicines and relevant laboratory results

blocks.text: [WhatsApp your complete medical file before travel](https://wa.me/919044346292?text=I%20would%20like%20to%20send%20my%20breast%20cancer%20diagnosis%20records%20for%20review%20before%20travelling%20to%20India.)
Should International Patients Repeat All Tests in India?
Not necessarily. The Indian treating team may accept existing investigations if they are sufficiently recent, technically adequate and clinically appropriate.

However, doctors may recommend repeating certain tests when reports are incomplete, imaging quality is inadequate, the treatment plan requires updated information, pathology requires confirmation, or the previous test is too old. Patients should not assume that every test will automatically need to be repeated.
Can Biopsy Samples Be Reviewed in India?

Yes, in appropriate circumstances, a hospital may review existing pathology material. Patients should ask the receiving hospital whether they require original pathology slides, paraffin tissue blocks, digital pathology files or original reports.

If the hospital requests physical pathology material, patients should follow its instructions for safe transport and documentation. Hospitals in [Delhi NCR](/hospitals/India/Delhi-NCR), [Mumbai](/hospitals/India/Mumbai), [Bengaluru](/hospitals/India/Bengaluru), [Chennai](/hospitals/India/Chennai) and [Hyderabad](/hospitals/India/Hyderabad) can advise what to send.
How Diagnosis Determines Treatment
The diagnostic process ultimately leads to a treatment plan. These are examples, not universal treatment pathways.

**Hormone receptor-positive breast cancer** may involve [surgery](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Lumpectomy), [radiation](/costs/India/Radiation-Oncology/EBRT), [hormone therapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Hormone-Therapy), [chemotherapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Chemotherapy) in selected patients, and other systemic treatment where appropriate.
**HER2-positive breast cancer** may involve surgery, chemotherapy, [HER2-targeted therapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Targeted-Therapy), radiation, and hormone therapy if ER/PR-positive.
**Triple-negative breast cancer** may involve surgery, chemotherapy, radiation and [immunotherapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Immunotherapy) in selected settings.
[Start the Breast Cancer Treatment in India pathway](/consult?treatment=Breast%20Cancer%20Treatment%20in%20India)
How Long Does Breast Cancer Diagnosis Take?
The timeline varies depending on the number of tests required. A straightforward pathway may include imaging → biopsy → pathology → receptor testing → treatment planning.

More complex cases may require additional imaging, repeat pathology review, additional biomarker testing and multidisciplinary discussion. International patients should therefore avoid booking a very short trip based only on the assumption that diagnosis and treatment planning will be completed in a single day.
Breast Cancer Diagnosis and Cost in India

The cost of diagnosis varies according to the investigations required. Potential components include consultation, mammography, ultrasound, MRI, biopsy, histopathology, immunohistochemistry, HER2 testing, blood tests, CT/PET-CT and other staging investigations.

Not every patient requires all of these tests. The final diagnostic cost depends on the patient's symptoms, existing records and clinical findings. See the [breast cancer treatment cost guide](/blogs/breast-cancer-treatment-cost-in-india) for how diagnosis sits next to [surgery](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Mastectomy), [chemotherapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Chemotherapy) and other treatment costs.
[Request a diagnosis and treatment estimate](/consult?treatment=Breast%20Cancer%20Treatment%20in%20India)
Questions to Ask Your Doctor After a Breast Cancer Diagnosis
Patients should consider asking:

items: What type of breast cancer do I have?
Do I need additional staging scans?
Do I need genetic or molecular testing?
Will I need targeted therapy or immunotherapy?
Should I obtain a second pathology opinion?
What should I do before travelling for treatment?

blocks.text: Frequently Asked Questions
Can a mammogram confirm breast cancer?
A mammogram can identify suspicious abnormalities, but a biopsy is generally required to establish a tissue diagnosis.
Is a biopsy always required?
When imaging or clinical findings are suspicious for cancer, tissue sampling is commonly required to establish the diagnosis. The exact approach depends on the clinical situation.
What is the difference between biopsy and pathology?
A biopsy is the process of obtaining tissue. Pathology is the examination of that tissue by a pathologist to determine what it contains and its characteristics.
What do ER and PR mean?
ER and PR refer to estrogen and progesterone receptors. Their presence can indicate that endocrine therapy may be useful.
What does HER2-positive mean?
It means the breast cancer meets the accepted criteria for increased HER2 activity based on tumour testing. HER2-positive cancers may be treated with HER2-targeted medicines.
What does triple-negative breast cancer mean?
It means the cancer does not express estrogen receptors, progesterone receptors or HER2.
Is HER2 2+ positive?
An IHC result of 2+ is generally considered equivocal rather than definitively positive and may require additional HER2 testing.
Does a breast lump always mean cancer?
No. Many breast lumps are benign. However, a new or persistent lump should be evaluated by a healthcare professional.
Can breast cancer be detected before symptoms appear?
Yes. Screening can detect some breast cancers before they produce noticeable symptoms.
Can international patients send pathology reports to India before travelling?

Yes, hospitals and medical teams may review medical records before an international patient's arrival. The exact documents accepted and whether additional testing is required should be confirmed with the receiving hospital.
Should I bring my biopsy slides to India?
Sometimes. The receiving hospital may request the original slides or tissue blocks for pathology review. Confirm this before travelling.
Does every breast cancer patient need a PET-CT?
No. Staging investigations depend on the clinical situation. A PET-CT is not automatically required for every breast cancer patient.
Breast Cancer Diagnosis: Key Takeaways
An accurate breast cancer diagnosis requires more than identifying a lump or abnormal scan. The diagnostic pathway may include:
Clinical examination → Imaging → Biopsy → Histopathology → ER/PR/HER2 testing → Staging → Multidisciplinary treatment planning
The pathology report is particularly important because it identifies the tumour's biological characteristics and helps determine which treatments may be appropriate.

For international patients travelling to India, sending the complete medical record before travel can help the receiving medical team review the diagnosis and identify any additional tests that may be required.

Quick answer

ER, PR and HER2 are biological markers used to classify breast cancer and guide treatment. ER means estrogen receptors, PR means progesterone receptors, and HER2 means human epidermal growth factor receptor 2. An ER-positive/HER2-negative cancer may be treated with endocrine therapy. blocks.text: ER, PR and HER2 are important biological markers used to classify breast cancer and guide treatment. ER refers to estrogen receptors, PR to progesterone receptors, and HER2 to human epidermal growth factor receptor 2.

A breast cancer may be ER-positive, PR-positive, HER2-positive, or have different combinations of these markers. These results help doctors determine whether treatments such as hormone therapy or HER2-targeted therapy may be appropriate.

For example, an ER-positive/HER2-negative cancer may be treated with [endocrine therapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Hormone-Therapy), while a HER2-positive cancer may be considered for [HER2-targeted treatment](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Targeted-Therapy). A cancer can also be both hormone receptor-positive and HER2-positive, in which case more than one type of systemic treatment may have a role.

ER, PR and HER2 results do not determine the complete treatment plan by themselves. Doctors also consider tumour size, lymph-node involvement, [stage](/blogs/breast-cancer-stages-0-1-2-3-4), tumour grade, menopausal status, previous treatment and other pathological findings. This explainer supports the [Breast Cancer Treatment in India](/treatments/breast-cancer-treatment-in-india) pathway, the [treatment-by-stage](/blogs/breast-cancer-treatment-by-stage) guide and the [cost guide](/blogs/breast-cancer-treatment-cost-in-india).

blocks.text: What Are ER, PR and HER2 in Breast Cancer?
Breast cancer is not a single disease. Two patients can both be diagnosed with breast cancer but have very different tumour biology and therefore require different treatment approaches.
Three of the most important biomarkers routinely discussed in breast cancer are:

items: HER2 — Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2

blocks.text: These markers are usually assessed using tissue obtained through a biopsy or surgery. The results help the oncology team understand how the cancer cells behave and which treatments may be useful.

In India, multidisciplinary teams in [Delhi NCR](/doctors/India/Delhi-NCR), [Mumbai](/doctors/India/Mumbai), [Bengaluru](/doctors/India/Bengaluru), [Chennai](/doctors/India/Chennai) and [Hyderabad](/doctors/India/Hyderabad) use these results together with stage and pathology to plan treatment.
What Does ER-Positive Breast Cancer Mean?
ER-positive breast cancer means that the cancer cells have estrogen receptors. Estrogen can stimulate the growth of some breast cancer cells.
When a tumour is ER-positive, treatment that interferes with estrogen signalling may be useful. This is known as endocrine therapy or [hormone therapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Hormone-Therapy).
Common endocrine treatments include tamoxifen, anastrozole, letrozole, exemestane, and ovarian-function suppression in selected premenopausal patients.
The exact treatment depends on factors such as age, menopausal status, cancer stage, recurrence risk and previous treatment.

- [Hormone Therapy Doctors in India](/doctors/India/Medical-Oncology/Hormone-Therapy)
- [Hormone Therapy Cost in India](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Hormone-Therapy)
[Ask whether hormone therapy applies](/consult?treatment=Hormone%20Therapy)
What Does PR-Positive Breast Cancer Mean?
PR stands for progesterone receptor. A PR-positive result means the cancer cells have progesterone receptors.

PR status is interpreted alongside ER status and other tumour characteristics. For example, a pathology report may describe a tumour as ER-positive / PR-positive, ER-positive / PR-negative, ER-negative / PR-positive, or ER-negative / PR-negative.
The combination provides information about the biological characteristics of the tumour.
What Does Hormone Receptor-Positive Mean?
You may hear doctors use the term hormone receptor-positive breast cancer. This generally refers to breast cancer that expresses estrogen receptors and/or progesterone receptors.
Therefore: ER-positive and/or PR-positive → hormone receptor-positive. This distinction is important because hormone receptor-positive breast cancers may respond to endocrine treatment.
What Is HER2?
HER2 is a protein involved in signalling that helps cells grow and divide. Some breast cancers have abnormally increased HER2 activity.

These cancers are classified as HER2-positive when they meet the relevant testing criteria. HER2 status is important because HER2-positive breast cancers may respond to medicines specifically designed to [target the HER2 pathway](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Targeted-Therapy).

- [Targeted Therapy Doctors in India](/doctors/India/Medical-Oncology/Targeted-Therapy)
- [Targeted Therapy Cost in India](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Targeted-Therapy)
How Are ER, PR and HER2 Tested?

blocks.alt: Visual process from a core-needle biopsy and tissue cassette, through a microscope and stain scores, to a report that guides medicine or surgery
blocks.caption: The markers are read from tumour tissue. Equivocal HER2 stains may need a second laboratory method before treatment is chosen.

blocks.text: These biomarkers are generally assessed using tumour tissue. The tissue may come from a core needle biopsy, other biopsy procedures, or breast surgery.
The pathology laboratory examines the tumour and performs the relevant tests.
ER and PR
ER and PR are commonly evaluated using immunohistochemistry (IHC). The report may provide a percentage of tumour cells showing receptor expression and an intensity or scoring description.
HER2
HER2 is commonly assessed using IHC. Results may be reported as 0, 1+, 2+ or 3+.

An IHC 3+ result is generally considered HER2-positive. An IHC 2+ result is usually considered equivocal and may require additional testing, such as in situ hybridization (ISH). The final interpretation should come from the pathology report and treating team.
Why Are ER, PR and HER2 So Important?
These results can directly affect treatment decisions.

items: ER-positive may indicate a role for endocrine therapy.
PR-positive provides additional information about hormone receptor biology.
HER2-positive may indicate a role for HER2-targeted therapy.

blocks.text: The results are combined with other information to create the treatment plan. Doctors do not generally decide treatment based on one biomarker alone.
Common ER, PR and HER2 Combinations
Breast cancer can have different combinations of these biomarkers.

| ER | PR | HER2 | General biological classification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Positive | Positive | Negative | Hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative |
| Positive | Negative | Negative | Hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative |
| Negative | Positive | Negative | Hormone receptor-positive based on PR expression |
| Positive | Positive | Positive | Hormone receptor-positive and HER2-positive |
| Positive | Negative | Positive | Hormone receptor-positive and HER2-positive |
| Negative | Negative | Positive | HER2-positive |
| Negative | Negative | Negative | Triple-negative |
This table is a simplified explanation. The treating team may also consider additional pathological and molecular information.

blocks.alt: Four visual treatment pathways: hormone-receptor disease with pills, HER2-positive disease with a targeted vial, dual biology with both medicines, and triple-negative disease with a drip and shield
blocks.caption: Hormone therapy, HER2-directed medicines, both together, or chemotherapy with selected immunotherapy — the pathway follows the receptor pattern.

blocks.text: ER-Positive, PR-Positive, HER2-Negative Breast Cancer
This is a common biological category of breast cancer. The cancer expresses hormone receptors but does not meet the criteria for HER2-positive disease.

Treatment may include [surgery](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Lumpectomy), [radiation therapy](/costs/India/Radiation-Oncology/EBRT), [endocrine therapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Hormone-Therapy), [chemotherapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Chemotherapy) in selected patients, and other systemic treatments depending on the individual case.
Endocrine therapy is an important component for many patients with hormone receptor-positive disease.
ER-Positive, PR-Negative, HER2-Negative Breast Cancer
A tumour does not have to be positive for both ER and PR to be considered hormone receptor-positive. If the tumour is ER-positive but PR-negative, endocrine therapy may still have an important role.

The oncology team will consider ER expression, PR expression, HER2 status, tumour grade, tumour size, lymph-node status, stage and other pathological features. Therefore, a PR-negative result does not automatically mean that hormone therapy will not work.
ER-Negative, PR-Positive Breast Cancer
ER-negative/PR-positive results are less common. When this pattern appears, the pathology and clinical context may need careful review.

The treating team may consider whether additional testing or pathology review is appropriate. Patients should avoid interpreting one receptor result independently from the rest of the pathology report.
ER-Positive, HER2-Positive Breast Cancer
A breast cancer can be both hormone receptor-positive and HER2-positive. This is an important distinction.
Such a tumour may have two relevant treatment pathways: endocrine treatment because of hormone receptor expression, and HER2-targeted treatment because of HER2 positivity.
Depending on the stage and other factors, treatment may also include chemotherapy, surgery and radiation therapy. The exact sequence depends on the individual case.

blocks.label: Ask how dual-positive disease is treated

blocks.text: ER-Negative, PR-Negative, HER2-Positive Breast Cancer
This tumour does not express ER or PR but meets the criteria for HER2-positive disease. HER2-targeted treatment may therefore be an important part of systemic treatment.
Depending on stage and treatment setting, chemotherapy, surgery and radiation may also be involved.
What Is Triple-Negative Breast Cancer?
Triple-negative breast cancer is generally defined by the absence of estrogen receptors, progesterone receptors and HER2.

Because these three targets are absent, endocrine therapy and standard HER2-targeted therapy do not have the same role. Treatment can include [chemotherapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Chemotherapy), surgery, [radiation therapy](/costs/India/Radiation-Oncology/EBRT), [immunotherapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Immunotherapy) in selected situations, and other systemic treatment where appropriate.

- [Chemotherapy Doctors in India](/doctors/India/Medical-Oncology/Chemotherapy)
- [Chemotherapy Cost in India](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Chemotherapy)
- [Immunotherapy Doctors in India](/doctors/India/Medical-Oncology/Immunotherapy)
- [Immunotherapy Cost in India](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Immunotherapy)
[Ask about triple-negative treatment options](/consult?treatment=Immunotherapy)
Does ER/PR/HER2 Status Determine the Stage?

blocks.alt: Split visual: a cell with receptors and medicines on the left, and a torso with local, nodal and distant organ spread on the right
blocks.caption: Biology describes what the tumour is like. Stage describes how far it has spread. Both are needed for a treatment plan.

blocks.text: No. This is an important distinction. Biomarker status and cancer stage are different things.

**Biomarkers** describe biological characteristics of the tumour. **[Stage](/blogs/breast-cancer-stages-0-1-2-3-4)** describes how extensive the cancer is — tumour size, lymph-node involvement and distant spread.
A patient can therefore have Stage 1, 2, 3 or 4 ER-positive cancer. The treatment plan can be very different even though the tumour has the same receptor status.
Does ER/PR/HER2 Status Affect Breast Cancer Treatment?
Yes. These results are important components of treatment planning.

ER-positive / HER2-negative disease may include endocrine therapy. HER2-positive disease may include HER2-targeted treatment. Triple-negative disease may rely more heavily on chemotherapy and, in selected situations, immunotherapy.
However, these are broad categories rather than individual treatment prescriptions.
ER, PR and HER2 Results After a Biopsy
The initial biopsy may establish the diagnosis and provide receptor information. However, surgery can provide additional tissue for pathology.
The surgical pathology report may provide information about final tumour size, histological type, tumour grade, lymph-node status, margins, ER, PR, HER2 and other pathological features.
Sometimes additional testing or review is necessary after surgery.
Can HER2 Results Change Between Biopsy and Surgery?
Biological characteristics can sometimes show differences between samples. This is one reason pathology is an important part of ongoing treatment planning.

If there is an unexpected result or a result that does not fit the overall clinical picture, doctors may consider repeat or confirmatory testing. Patients should discuss any difference between biopsy and surgical pathology with their treating oncologist and pathologist.
What Is the Role of Ki-67?
Ki-67 is a marker of cell proliferation. It can provide information about how actively tumour cells are dividing. It may appear on a breast cancer pathology report.
However, Ki-67 is different from ER, PR and HER2. It should not be interpreted in isolation. Its clinical usefulness can vary depending on the specific treatment situation and laboratory methodology.
ER/PR/HER2 and Breast Cancer Treatment by Stage
Stage 0

Stage 0 includes non-invasive disease such as DCIS. Treatment may involve [breast-conserving surgery](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Lumpectomy), [mastectomy](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Mastectomy) in selected situations, [radiation](/costs/India/Radiation-Oncology/EBRT) after breast-conserving surgery, and endocrine therapy in selected hormone receptor-positive cases.
Stage 1

Early-stage invasive breast cancer may be treated with surgery, radiation where indicated, endocrine therapy if hormone receptor-positive, HER2-targeted treatment if HER2-positive, and chemotherapy in selected patients. The exact treatment depends on tumour size, biology and other risk factors.
Stage 2

Stage 2 disease may require a combination of surgery, chemotherapy, HER2-targeted therapy, radiation and endocrine therapy. The sequence may vary. Some patients receive systemic therapy before surgery.
Stage 3

Locally advanced breast cancer often requires multimodal treatment. Depending on tumour biology, treatment may involve systemic therapy before surgery, surgery, radiation, endocrine therapy, HER2-targeted therapy and other systemic treatments. The exact sequence is individualized.
Stage 4
Stage 4 breast cancer has spread to distant parts of the body. Treatment is primarily systemic and depends heavily on tumour biology.

Hormone receptor-positive disease may receive endocrine-based treatment. HER2-positive disease may receive HER2-directed treatment. Triple-negative disease may be treated with chemotherapy and selected immunotherapy or other systemic approaches. Treatment can change over time depending on response and disease progression.
For how stage changes the sequence, read [Breast Cancer Stages 0–4](/blogs/breast-cancer-stages-0-1-2-3-4) and [treatment by stage](/blogs/breast-cancer-treatment-by-stage).
How Does Hormone Therapy Work in ER-Positive Breast Cancer?

Hormone therapy aims to reduce the ability of estrogen to stimulate cancer cells. Depending on the medicine, it may block estrogen receptors, reduce estrogen production, or suppress ovarian estrogen production.
**Tamoxifen** blocks estrogen's effects in breast tissue.
**Aromatase inhibitors** such as anastrozole, letrozole and exemestane reduce estrogen production and are commonly used in postmenopausal patients.
**Ovarian-function suppression** may be used in selected premenopausal patients, sometimes together with another endocrine medicine.
How Does HER2-Targeted Therapy Work?
HER2-targeted medicines are designed to interfere with HER2-driven signalling. Examples include trastuzumab, pertuzumab, trastuzumab emtansine and trastuzumab deruxtecan.

The medicine used depends on the treatment setting. For example, the treatment of newly diagnosed early-stage disease can differ substantially from treatment of metastatic disease that has already received HER2-directed therapy.
Can a Patient Receive Both Hormone Therapy and HER2-Targeted Therapy?
Yes. This can occur when a breast cancer is both hormone receptor-positive and HER2-positive. The patient may receive a treatment plan that addresses both biological pathways.
Depending on the stage, this can include chemotherapy + HER2-targeted therapy + surgery + radiation + endocrine therapy. Not every patient needs all of these treatments.
How Does the Treatment Team Decide What Comes First?

Treatment sequencing depends on stage, tumour size, lymph-node involvement, ER/PR status, HER2 status, tumour grade, the patient's health, menopausal status, planned surgery, need for radiation and previous treatment.
Some patients undergo surgery first. Others receive systemic treatment before surgery. This is known as neoadjuvant treatment.

blocks.label: Ask whether treatment should start before surgery

blocks.text: Why Is Neoadjuvant Treatment Used?
Neoadjuvant treatment is treatment given before the main local treatment, usually surgery. It may include chemotherapy, HER2-targeted therapy and endocrine therapy in selected situations.

Potential reasons include shrinking the tumour, treating microscopic disease early, assessing treatment response and helping determine subsequent treatment. The decision depends on the patient's specific cancer.
Does Hormone Receptor Status Affect Chemotherapy Decisions?

It can be one of several factors considered. Doctors may evaluate ER/PR status, HER2 status, tumour size, grade, lymph nodes, menopausal status and other pathological or genomic information where appropriate.

For some hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative cancers, additional genomic testing may help inform chemotherapy decisions. Whether such testing is useful depends on the individual clinical situation.
Do All ER-Positive Patients Need Chemotherapy?
No. ER-positive breast cancer can range from very small, lower-risk tumours to more advanced or biologically aggressive cancers. Chemotherapy decisions depend on multiple factors.

Some patients may receive surgery, radiation and endocrine therapy, while others may require chemotherapy as well. The treatment plan should be based on the complete pathology and clinical assessment.
Do All HER2-Positive Patients Need the Same Treatment?

No. HER2-positive breast cancer includes different clinical situations. Treatment can vary according to tumour size, lymph-node status, stage, whether treatment is before or after surgery, previous HER2-targeted therapy, and whether the disease is metastatic.
Therefore, the term "HER2-positive" alone is not enough to determine the entire treatment regimen.
What Should International Patients Know About ER, PR and HER2?
For patients travelling to India for treatment, these reports are particularly important. Before travelling, collect:

The Indian treating team can use these records to understand the previous diagnosis and treatment. GAF Healthcare coordinates this review with teams in [Delhi NCR](/hospitals/India/Delhi-NCR), [Mumbai](/hospitals/India/Mumbai), [Bengaluru](/hospitals/India/Bengaluru), [Chennai](/hospitals/India/Chennai) and [Hyderabad](/hospitals/India/Hyderabad).

blocks.label: WhatsApp your pathology for a biomarker review

blocks.text: Should International Patients Repeat ER, PR and HER2 Testing in India?
Not necessarily. The treating hospital may accept existing reports.

However, repeat or confirmatory testing may be considered if the report is incomplete, the testing methodology is unclear, the result is equivocal, the result is unexpected, the treatment decision depends on confirmation, or the pathology material needs specialist review.
Patients should ask the receiving hospital before travelling whether additional testing is expected.
What Does an ER/PR/HER2 Pathology Report Look Like?
A simplified report might contain information such as:

| Marker | Example result |
| --- | --- |
| ER | Positive |
| PR | Positive |
| HER2 IHC | 0 / 1+ / 2+ / 3+ |
| HER2 ISH | If required |
| Tumour grade | Grade 1, 2 or 3 |
| Histological type | e.g. invasive carcinoma |
The exact format varies between laboratories. A patient should have the complete report interpreted by the treating medical team rather than relying on one line.
Questions to Ask Your Oncologist
After receiving the pathology report, consider asking:

items: Is my cancer ER-positive or ER-negative?
Does my HER2 result require confirmatory testing?
Should I have genomic or molecular testing?
Should I have a pathology second opinion?

blocks.text: Frequently Asked Questions
What does ER-positive breast cancer mean?
It means the cancer cells express estrogen receptors. Endocrine therapy may therefore be an important part of treatment.
What does PR-positive breast cancer mean?
It means the cancer cells express progesterone receptors. PR status is interpreted alongside ER, HER2 and other tumour characteristics.
What does HER2-positive mean?
It means the tumour meets accepted criteria for increased HER2 activity based on pathology testing. HER2-targeted medicines may therefore be considered.
Can breast cancer be ER-positive and HER2-positive?
Yes. A tumour can express hormone receptors and also be HER2-positive.
Can breast cancer be ER-positive but PR-negative?
Yes. ER and PR are separate biomarkers, so they can have different results.
What does triple-negative mean?
Triple-negative breast cancer lacks estrogen receptors, progesterone receptors and HER2 according to the relevant testing criteria.
Does HER2-positive mean the cancer is Stage 4?
No. HER2 status and stage are different characteristics. A HER2-positive cancer can be diagnosed at an early stage or at an advanced stage.
Does ER-positive mean the cancer is less serious?
ER status alone cannot determine how serious a cancer is. Stage, tumour biology and multiple other factors are important.
Does every ER-positive patient need hormone therapy?
Endocrine therapy is commonly considered for hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, but the final treatment plan depends on the individual clinical situation.
Does every HER2-positive patient need trastuzumab?
Trastuzumab has an important role in many HER2-positive breast cancer treatment settings, but whether it is appropriate and how it is used depends on the individual diagnosis and previous treatment.
Can ER, PR or HER2 status change?
Tumour biology can sometimes differ between samples or between the original tumour and recurrent/metastatic disease. When clinically appropriate, doctors may recommend reassessment.
Can international patients have their pathology reviewed in India?
Yes. A hospital may review pathology reports and, where necessary, the original slides or tissue blocks.

blocks.text: ER, PR and HER2: Key Takeaways
ER, PR and HER2 are among the most important biomarkers used in breast cancer treatment planning.
**ER** indicates estrogen receptor expression and can identify patients who may benefit from endocrine therapy.
**PR** provides additional information about hormone receptor biology.
**HER2** identifies cancers that may benefit from HER2-targeted treatment.
Importantly, these markers should never be interpreted separately from cancer stage and the rest of the pathology report.

A complete breast cancer treatment plan may involve surgery, chemotherapy, radiation therapy, hormone therapy, HER2-targeted therapy and immunotherapy in selected situations. The combination and sequence depend on the individual patient.

For international patients considering treatment in India, sending the complete pathology and imaging records before travel can help the receiving oncology team understand the diagnosis and plan the next steps.

blocks.html:
Quick answer

Breast cancer stage describes how extensive the cancer is. Doctors consider tumour size and local extent, nearby lymph-node involvement and whether the cancer has spread to distant organs. Stage 0 is usually non-invasive disease such as DCIS. Stages 1–3 are invasive cancers with increasing local or regional extent. Stage 4 is metastatic disease. Stage is only one part of the plan: ER, PR, HER2, grade and overall health can change treatment even when two patients share a stage.

blocks.text: Breast cancer stage describes how extensive the cancer is in the body. Doctors primarily consider the size and extent of the breast tumour, nearby lymph-node involvement and whether the cancer has spread to distant organs.

Breast cancer is commonly grouped into Stage 0, Stage 1, Stage 2, Stage 3 and Stage 4. Stage 0 generally refers to non-invasive disease such as ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS), while Stages 1–3 describe invasive breast cancers with increasing local or regional extent. Stage 4 means the cancer has spread to distant parts of the body and is also called metastatic breast cancer.

Stage is only one part of the diagnosis. Doctors also consider ER, PR and HER2 status, tumour grade, histological type, lymph-node findings, genomic or molecular information when appropriate, overall health and previous treatment.

Treatment can include [surgery](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Lumpectomy), [chemotherapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Chemotherapy), [radiation therapy](/costs/India/Radiation-Oncology/EBRT), [hormone therapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Hormone-Therapy), [HER2-targeted therapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Targeted-Therapy), [immunotherapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Immunotherapy) or combinations of these. The same stage does not necessarily mean the same treatment for every patient. This explainer supports the [Breast Cancer Treatment in India](/treatments/breast-cancer-treatment-in-india) pathway, the [treatment-by-stage](/blogs/breast-cancer-treatment-by-stage) guide and the [cost guide](/blogs/breast-cancer-treatment-cost-in-india).
